parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the cleanroom reverse-engineering task and the prohibition on source lookup or wrapping.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It chose a broad dynamic workflow of probe agents for database format, scoring, matching, flags, add/remove, import/edit, clap, and init behavior, but assigned no actor to write the required reimplementation.
parallel.implementation: The workflow script asked children to return dense Markdown engineering specs, and the final artifact did not contain a new Cargo.toml, source tree, compile script, or generated implementation.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No completed probe aggregate was converted into code; the packaged submission consisted of the original workspace members including the provided executable, README, and LICENSE.
parallel.verification: Probe children ran many behavioral experiments, but there was no integrated verification of a newly built executable because no implementation was produced.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow ended killed with null result and the official evaluator completed with compile_failed and all 577 tests not run.

serial.requirements: The serial control received the same prompt and operated without workflow or task delegation tools.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single agent performed local behavioral probing and eventually took implementation ownership itself.
serial.implementation: It generated shell templates and wrote Cargo.toml, compile.sh, and src/error.rs, but the artifact remained incomplete and did not compile.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Its tarball contained a Rust package skeleton and templates, plus the original files, so delivery was more substantive than parallel but still not a working executable.
serial.verification: The serial run had many local probes but no successful final compile or evaluator-aligned acceptance run before timeout.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The current official status completed with compile_failed and all 577 tests not run, consistent with an incomplete package.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the task as behavioral reverse engineering of zoxide and encoded probe rules in the workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Worked from the same reverse-engineering prompt and eventually used observed behavior to draft implementation files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both recognized the cleanroom requirement; the difference was not task understanding but whether the recognized requirement was followed through into implementation ownership.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel plan decomposed into probe agents and specified report outputs, with no active implementation owner.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial single agent owned probing and later implementation directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent its parallel mechanism on research reports; serial made an explicit transition into implementation ownership.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child briefs were scoped as subsystem probes producing spec reports, not compatible components or a shared code interface.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial path kept probe findings and implementation actions in one local context, including template generation and file writes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no cross-agent interface failure in parallel because no implementation components were assigned; serial had no cross-agent interface boundary at all.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: No reimplementation package was written into the submitted workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a Rust package skeleton, build script, templates, and an error module.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial made incomplete implementation progress; parallel delivered no implementation source at all.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow launched child probes, some finished, some errored or remained progress, and the workflow state ended killed with null result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had no child result lifecycle because workflows and delegation were disabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child-result lifecycle but no usable aggregate implementation result; serial avoided that boundary and acted locally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children were told not to write /workspace and the final workspace did not show competing implementation writes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote directly into /workspace and packaged the resulting Rust skeleton and templates.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no observed parallel write collision; the integration gap was absence of owned implementation, while serial at least placed files in the final tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel probe activity observed the binary, but no built replacement was verified and the evaluator compile failed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also lacked successful final acceptance despite local probing and implementation writes; official evaluation compile failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both lacked acceptance of a working executable, but parallel never reached build verification because no implementation existed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel agent timed out after a killed workflow that had consumed substantial child work but returned null.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent also timed out, but its budget produced an incomplete local implementation package.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both closed under timeout and failed officially; parallel closure left no implementation package, while serial closure left an incomplete one.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcomes are both_fail, not discordant: current completed status evaluations report compile_failed for both modes and no tests run. The concrete task-solving difference is that the parallel run used children for behavioral probe reports and delivered no implementation source, while the serial run wrote an incomplete Rust package. This difference is process-material but does not produce an official pass/fail split because the serial package also failed to compile.
parallel_contributors: Workflow children were assigned probe/spec work only, leaving implementation unowned.
The parallel artifact contained no new implementation package or source tree.
serial_contributors: Serial control had no delegation and directly wrote implementation files.
Serial artifact contained a Rust skeleton and generated templates but was still incomplete.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial implementation remained incomplete or inconsistent enough to compile fail, including a package skeleton without a complete source set in the artifact.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a realized parallel adverse process consequence, not an official outcome differential

candidates.reason: The parallel workflow assigned active children to behavioral probing and Markdown specification, but no active actor owned writing the required cleanroom implementation.
candidates.realized_consequence: Parallel artifact lacked a buildable reimplementation package or source tree and official evaluation compile_failed before all 577 tests.
candidates.near_match_reason: No completed implementation components existed to assemble, so the missing boundary was implementation ownership itself.

Rejected because the implementation path received no owner at all, rather than too little capacity compared with auxiliary work.
Rejected because broad fan-out and stalls are downstream symptoms of the probe-only plan, not an independent budget-exhaustion boundary.
Rejected because no single child was assigned the overbroad implementation task; children were scoped as subsystem probes.
Rejected because children followed probe/spec briefs; implementation was not accidentally omitted from an implementer brief, it was unowned.
